title: French Dressing
subtitle: Classic vinaigrette with Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar
excerpt: The foundation dressing for every green salad: a sharp, mustard-thickened emulsion of red wine vinegar and olive oil. Quick to make, endlessly useful, and far better made fresh than from a bottle.

recipe.sourceNotes: Vinaigrette is one of the basic preparations of French cuisine, a simple oil-and-vinegar emulsion stabilised by the lecithin in Dijon mustard. The classic French ratio is three parts oil to one part vinegar, though this varies by taste and the acidity of the vinegar: a sharper dressing suits a robust salad (frisée, watercress) while a milder dressing suits delicate leaves. The mustard is not optional: it is the emulsifier that keeps the dressing from splitting immediately. A true vinaigrette (from the French vinaigre, vinegar) is freshly made and lightly dressed: in French tradition, salad leaves are barely coated, not drenched. The proportion of dressing to leaves is a common source of overdressed salads in home cooking: 1 tablespoon of dressing is enough for a large handful of leaves. The dressing keeps for one week in a jar in the fridge and should be shaken or re-whisked before each use.

content.text: The mustard goes in first because it is the emulsifier: whisk or shake the mustard, vinegar, and salt together thoroughly before adding the oil. Add the oil slowly while whisking, or add everything to a jar and shake vigorously for 30 seconds. The dressing should be opaque and thickened rather than separated and oily. Taste before dressing any salad: the balance between acid and oil should lean slightly sharp, because leaves dilute the dressing when tossed.
Put the mustard, vinegar, salt, and pepper in a jar or small bowl. Whisk or stir until combined. Add the garlic if using.

Slowly drizzle in the olive oil while whisking constantly, or add to the jar and shake vigorously for 30 seconds until the dressing is emulsified and opaque. Taste: it should be noticeably sharp. Adjust the vinegar, salt, or a pinch of sugar as needed.
Use immediately or store in a jar in the fridge for up to one week. Shake well before each use. Dress salad leaves sparingly: a tablespoon per generous serving is usually sufficient.
